text:
jordan_seely: forwarding — ACME reported their billing for April (invoice) is ~900k tokens but the usage dashboard shows ~1.2M for project acme-prod. customer very confused, says charges don't match dashboard screenshot. attaching convo + sample request_ids.

alex_chan: thanks — can you paste the project_id + any sample request IDs and the exact invoice period (start/end)? also was the customer looking at per-project dashboard or org-level? :thinking:

jordan_seely: project_id: proj-acme-9
sample request ids: 64b2f1a8, 64b2f2b3, 64b3001e
invoice period: 2024-04-01 to 2024-04-30 (calendar month)
they viewed the project dashboard (project view), screenshot shows "30d window" on top.

samira_ruiz: quick note: invoices are monthly calendar buckets and are billed at the org level (we sum across projects). the UI dashboard has multiple modes: calendar-month view, and a rolling 30d sliding window — those can differ, especially near month boundaries. could that explain the delta?

jordan_seely: customer insists the dashboard was the project calendar month view. they also say numbers in the API usage csv export don't match invoice. they provided the csv (link hidden) and a screenshot.

alex_chan: ok can we repro? maya, can you check how the project dashboard aggregates tokens vs the invoice pipeline? specifically: per-project aggregation + rolling-window edge cases + whether shared tokens from org-level routes get double-counted.

maya_ng: looking. quick finding: we recently merged change to "workspace-level aggregation" which alters how requests tagged with both project_id and workspace_id are counted. new aggregator should prefer project_id only, but there's a fallback path that increments both project and workspace counters for some batched requests — will run a repro now.

maya_ng: repro steps I'm using:
1) run a small script hitting the /v1/generate endpoint with header `X-Project-ID: proj-acme-9` and `X-Workspace-ID: ws-acme`.
2) send 3 requests with different prompt lengths (100, 800, 400 tokens).
3) check counts via admin query: `SELECT sum(tokens) FROM usage_events WHERE project_id='proj-acme-9' AND time >= '2024-04-01' AND time <= '2024-04-30'`

maya_ng: found two issues: 1) rolling-window endpoint used in the project dashboard was using window_end = now() and window_start = now()-30d (sliding) even when UI said "calendar month" due to a client-side flag mismatch. 2) aggregation path: when a request included both project & workspace headers and hit batching layer, one code path emitted two usage_events records (one with project_id set, one with workspace_id set) and the billing pipeline dedup only removes identical event_ids — not cross-dimension duplicates. this results in inflated dashboard numbers for some projects.

samira_ruiz: that explains some of the uplift; invoices dedupe differently because the billing pipeline groups by org_id and sums unique event_ids after normalization. so dashboard (project view) can overcount in this bad path while invoice dedup path collapses the workspace duplicate, leading to lower invoice numbers.

alex_chan: do we have a short-term mitigation for ACME while we fix the code? can we offer them an export that matches invoice logic so they can reconcile?

maya_ng: short term:
- ops_admin can run the normalized export used by billing: `/internal/exports/usage?org=acme&start=2024-04-01&end=2024-04-30&mode=invoice-normalized`
- UI workaround: switch dashboard to "Org view" and set calendar month filter (matches billing rollup).
I'll push a hotfix to the batching emitter to stop emitting the duplicate workspace event. patch ready, running unit tests.

ops_bot: deployment queued: canary -> staging -> prod (hotfix/duplicate-usage-event) by maya_ng — CI checks passed. :rocket:

maya_ng: patch deployed to staging, ran the repro script: staging shows tokens = sum(expected) and no duplicate events in the raw usage table.

samira_ruiz: i created internal ticket BILL-1724 to flag affected invoices/customers and list reconciliation steps. adding ACME as P1 for manual audit.

alex_chan: sent ACME: "we've identified two causes (UI filter mismatch and duplicate emitter events). temporary reconciliation export available; engineering pushed a fix to stop duplicates and we're rolling canary now. we'll follow up once prod is healthy and offer credit if needed."

jordan_seely: customer replied: thanks, will wait for the reconciliation export and let us know if they want credit.

maya_ng: canary passed, rolling to prod now. expect propagated fix in ~15 mins. I'll post back with verification query.

maya_ng: verification query (run after 15m):
```
SELECT
  project_id,
  date_trunc('day', time) as d,
  sum(tokens) as tokens_per_day
FROM usage_events
WHERE project_id='proj-acme-9' AND time >= '2024-04-01' AND time < '2024-05-01'
GROUP BY project_id, d
ORDER BY d;
```

ops_bot: deploy to prod succeeded for hotfix/duplicate-usage-event. :white_check_mark:

maya_ng: prod shows numbers now matching the invoice-normalized export for proj-acme-9. i've added extra unit tests and a quick E2E that validates the emitter doesn't create cross-dimension duplicates.

samira_ruiz: i've sent the reconciliation export to ACME and added notes on why the dashboard and invoice diverged (UI filter label + emitter bug). also noted they can request a usage recheck.

alex_chan: thanks team. can someone add a short blurb in docs about the difference between "30d rolling" vs "calendar month" and that org-level invoices may dedupe some events differently? small doc + changelog entry.

maya_ng: will open DOCS-459 for the blurb, linking BILL-1724.

jordan_seely: ACME confirmed reconciliation matches invoice after export. they'll request credit if any gap remains. closing thread once billing confirms. :thumbsup:

samira_ruiz: marking this resolved from billing side, follow up if customer asks for credit.

alex_chan: closing loop — great cross-team work. :clap:
